Hexaploid wheat and tetraploid wheat undergo sexual hybridization to obtain F1. A microscopic photograph of chromosomes during meiosis of F1 pollen mother cells is shown in the figure. Question: How many chromosomes are there in F1 somatic cells?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Sexual hybridization can cultivate offspring whose comprehensive traits are superior to those of both parents, and is an important method of plant breeding. Hexaploid wheat and tetraploid wheat undergo sexual hybridization to obtain F1. A microscopic photograph of chromosomes during meiosis of F1 pollen mother cells is shown in the figure. Question: How many chromosomes are there in F1 somatic cells?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the microscopic photograph, two types of chromosome morphology can be seen. One type is clustered, paired synapsed structures, labeled in the figure as “tetrad”; the other type is isolated rod-like structures, labeled in the figure as “single chromosome.” According to the morphology in the figure, during meiosis of the F1 pollen mother cell, there are 14 tetrads and 7 single chromosomes. Reasoning: During meiosis, one tetrad corresponds to a pair of homologous chromosomes, that is, 2 chromosomes; one single chromosome corresponds to 1 unpaired chromosome. Therefore, the total number of chromosomes in the F1 cell is 14×2+7=35 chromosomes. The pollen mother cell comes from an F1 somatic cell, so the chromosome number of F1 somatic cells is also 35 chromosomes.
